Fit one linear mixed model per feature, with a random intercept for each group of samples

stats_fit_mixed.Rd

Fit one linear mixed model per feature of a feature-by-sample table, with a random intercept per group of samples (dataset, donor, day), and test each named coefficient with a Wald t.

mzLib's MixedModel.Fit models y = X beta + u_group + e for every feature separately: the fixed effects in your design, plus one baseline per group (a dataset, a donor, an acquisition day) drawn from N(0, tau^2). Each coefficient is tested by a two-sided Wald t on nlme's "containment" degrees of freedom. It is nlme::lme(y ~ ..., random = ~ 1 | group) per feature, which mzLib reproduces to 1e-5 relative (nlme's own precision), with identical df.

Usage

stats_fit_mixed(responses, design, groups, coefficients, estimator = NULL, threads = 1,
  timeout = 600)

Arguments

responses

stats_fit's responses table: a TSV with a header row, the feature id first, then one column per sample, named by its header. Log-transform intensities first. Blank, NA or NaN is missing; 0 is an observation.

design

stats_fit's design: one row per sample, the sample name then one numeric column per fixed-effect coefficient. Do not add a column per group: the random intercept replaces it.

groups

A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name (exactly the responses' samples, in any order), then ONE column with the sample's group label, whose header names the grouping (day, donor, dataset).

coefficients

Design column names to report, each as one block of rows. Every design column is fitted whatever you name.

estimator

"reml" or "ml": how the variances are estimated. Leave it NULL for mzLib's default ("reml" at mzLib d10017ce); estimator in the result says which was used. "ml" gives log-likelihoods you can compare between designs.

threads

Features fitted at once (threads), or -1 for every core. The answer is identical at any value.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

Use it when samples come in groups that share a baseline - runs acquired on the same day, replicates of one donor, studies in a pooled analysis - and you want each coefficient's effect *within* groups. stats_fit treats every sample as independent, so a day-to-day shift there either inflates the residual variance or, if the days are unbalanced, leaks into the effect.

Value

An mzlibr_mixed_model_fit:

- records, a data.frame with one row per (reported coefficient, feature) - one block of feature_count rows per coefficient you named, in that order: feature; coefficient; status; estimate, the fixed effect within groups in response units per coefficient unit (a log2 fold change for a 0/1 column on log2 intensities); standard_error (response units per coefficient unit); df (degrees of freedom), nlme's containment df, a whole number, NA when not fitted or when no positive df exists (a group-level coefficient with too few groups); t (standard errors), the Wald statistic; p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), two-sided on df, not adjusted across features, NA also when df is; residual_variance (squared response units), sigma^2 within groups; group_variance (squared response units), tau^2 between the groups' baselines, where 0 is the boundary (no group effect); log_likelihood (log-likelihood), restricted under "reml"; observed, samples with a finite response; and groups, distinct groups among them. Statistics are NA where status is not "fitted". - responses_file, design_file and groups_file, as absolute paths; grouping, the groups file's label column header; group_names, in order of first appearance; group_count groups; feature_count features and sample_count samples read; sample_names; coefficient_names and tested_coefficients; estimator, the estimator mzLib used; threads; missing_count and zero_count response cells (cells); status_counts, features per status; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: what the model is and is not, plus counts for this input: unfitted features, rows with no df, features at the boundary, zero cells.

What it is not

A random intercept per group and nothing more: no random slopes, nested or crossed groupings, or residual correlation. Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger df (lmerTest, pbkrtest) are not implemented, so p-values differ from lmerTest's. A feature the fixed effects fit exactly is reported fitted, with a residual_variance at rounding level and a meaningless t and p_value: check residual_variance before trusting a very small p_value.

Wraps

Wire verb stats fit-mixed. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.fit-mixed.yaml (bridge commit 4e180efe8b59) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • MixedModel.Fit in mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • MixedModelFit in mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • VarianceEstimator in mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • FeatureFitStatus in mzLib/StatisticalModels/LinearModel.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

responses

path; required. stats fit's responses table. A TSV with a header row: the first column is the feature id (unique, any header) and every other column is one sample, named by its header. Cells are used as given, so log-transform intensities first. A blank cell, NA or NaN (any case) is missing and is omitted from that feature's fit, never imputed. A 0 is an OBSERVATION. Blank lines are skipped.

design

path; required. stats fit's design table: a TSV with a header row and one row per sample, the sample name (matching the responses header exactly, rows matched by name) then one column per fixed-effect coefficient, every cell a finite number. Include an intercept column if you want one; do not add a column per group, which the random intercept replaces. mzLib refuses a design that is not of full column rank over all samples.

groups

path; required. A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name, then EXACTLY ONE column, the sample's group label (a dataset accession, a donor, an acquisition day), whose header names the grouping. The sample names must be exactly the responses' sample columns, in any order. Labels are text, trimmed and compared exactly; NA is a label like any other. An empty label is refused by mzLib (MixedModel.Fit), naming the sample.

coefficients (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line; each a design column name, none repeated. The coefficients to report, one design column name per line. The model always fits every design column; the table holds one block of rows per coefficient named here, in this order.

estimator

string; default absent; range reml | ml. How the variances are estimated: reml is mzLib's VarianceEstimator.Reml (restricted maximum likelihood, not biased downward by the number of coefficients), ml is VarianceEstimator.MaximumLikelihood (biased variances in small samples, but log-likelihoods comparable between designs). Absent, the bridge sends none and MixedModel.Fit's default applies (Reml at d10017ce); the envelope's estimator says which was used.

threads

int; in threads; default 1; range >= 1, or -1 for every core. Features fitted at once. The bridge default is 1 (BULK.md); mzLib's own default is -1. Results are identical at any value (mzLib).

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

responses_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the responses table.

design_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the design table.

groups_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the groups table.

grouping

string; never NA. The groups file's label column header.

group_names

string[]; never NA. The distinct labels, in order of first appearance over the responses' samples (the order mzLib numbers them in).

group_count

int; in groups; never NA. Distinct labels over all samples. A feature's own count, over its observed samples, is its groups column.

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Feature rows read.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Sample columns read.

sample_names

string[]; never NA. In responses header order, which is the order the design and group rows were put in.

coefficient_names

string[]; never NA. Every design column, in order.

tested_coefficients

string[]; never NA. The stdin coefficients, in order; the table holds one block of feature_count rows per entry.

estimator

string; never NA. reml or ml: the estimator mzLib reports it fitted with (MixedModelFit.Estimator), the default when --estimator was absent.

threads

int; in threads; never NA. The thread count used.

missing_count

int; in cells; never NA. Response cells that were blank, NA or NaN.

zero_count

int; in cells; never NA. Response cells that are exactly 0, fitted as observations.

status_counts

map<string,int>; in features; never NA. Features per status, always these six keys: fitted, too_few_observations, rank_deficient, too_few_groups, variance_ratio_at_limit, not_converged. They are the outcomes MixedModel.Fit's body can return at d10017ce; a stop-gap until mzLib says per model (mzLib#1487).

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. feature_count x the number of tested coefficients.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (tested coefficient, feature): coefficient blocks in stdin order, features in file order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Seven static caveats (one of them says which estimator), plus one each, with counts, when any feature was not fitted, when a fitted row has no df, when a fitted feature's group_variance is 0, and when any cell is 0.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. The feature id from the responses file's first column.

coefficient

string; never NA. The coefficient this row reports.

status

string; never NA. fitted | too_few_observations (no more observed samples than coefficients) | rank_deficient (the design restricted to the observed samples is not of full rank) | too_few_groups (fewer than two observed groups, or no group observed twice, so group and residual variance cannot be told apart) | variance_ratio_at_limit (group_variance / residual_variance ran to the top of mzLib's search, e^12, typically near-identical replicates within each group) | not_converged (the likelihood at the chosen variance ratio could not be evaluated: a non-finite value, or a residual sum of squares of 0 or below). Only fitted rows carry statistics.

estimate

float; in response units per coefficient unit (e.g. log2 fold change for a 0/1 column on log2 intensities); NA when status is not fitted. The generalized-least-squares fixed-effect coefficient at the estimated variances: the effect within groups, each group keeping its own baseline.

standard_error

float; in response units per coefficient unit; NA when not fitted. sqrt of the diagonal of s^2 (X' V^-1 X)^-1 with s^2 = RSS / (observed - coefficients), under both estimators, as nlme's summary reports.

df

float; in degrees of freedom; NA when not fitted, or the containment df is not positive (a group-level coefficient with too few observed groups to test it). Denominator df of the t test, by nlme's containment rule for one grouping level, a whole number: observed - observed groups - within-group coefficients for a coefficient that varies within some group and for the intercept; observed groups - group-level coefficients, minus 1 more with an intercept, for one constant within every group.

t

float; in standard errors; NA when not fitted. Wald statistic, estimate / standard_error. Reported even when df is null.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted, or df is null. Two-sided p-value of the t test on df. Not adjusted across features.

residual_variance

float; in squared response units; NA when not fitted. sigma^2, the within-group variance: RSS / (observed - coefficients) under reml, RSS / observed under ml. The same in every coefficient block.

group_variance

float; in squared response units; NA when not fitted. tau^2, the between-group variance of the random intercept. 0 is the boundary estimate (no between-group variance), which nlme cannot reach and reports as a tiny positive value. The same in every coefficient block.

log_likelihood

float; in log-likelihood (natural log); NA when not fitted. The maximized log-likelihood, restricted under reml. The same in every coefficient block.

observed

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with a finite response for this feature.

groups

int; in groups; never NA. Distinct groups among this feature's observed samples.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

responses, design or groups missing, blank or not found; a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; the groups file with other than two columns or an empty label header; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample or coefficient name; a response cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a design cell that is not a finite number

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the design's or the groups' samples are not exactly the responses' sample columns (both differences are named); no coefficient on stdin, one named twice, or one not in the design; --estimator other than reml or ml, or without a value; --threads 0 or below -1

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a design not of full column rank; a sample whose group label is empty, named by 0-based position and then by its name

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • A random intercept per group and nothing more, as nlme::lme(y ~ ..., random = ~ 1 | group): no random slopes, nested or crossed groupings, or residual correlation.

  • Fixed effects are tested by Wald t on nlme's containment degrees of freedom. Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger (lmerTest, pbkrtest) are not implemented, so p-values differ from lmerTest's. mzLib matches nlme 3.1.169 to 1e-5 relative (nlme's own optimizer precision) in estimates, standard errors, variances, p-values and log-likelihoods, with identical df.

  • group_variance 0 is the boundary estimate. nlme works on the log scale, cannot reach 0, and reports a tiny positive value there instead.

  • Under reml, log_likelihood is the restricted log-likelihood: compare it only between models with the same fixed effects, and use --estimator ml to compare designs. Under ml, residual_variance is RSS / observed, but standard errors use RSS / (observed - coefficients), as nlme's summary reports ML fits.

  • p_value is not adjusted across features. Send one coefficient's p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

  • A 0 is an observation. Log-transform intensities first, and blank any cell that means 'not measured'.

  • A feature the fixed effects fit exactly (a constant one, say) is reported fitted, with a residual_variance at rounding level (about 1e-16) and a meaningless t and p_value: MixedModel's not_converged guard catches only a residual sum of squares of exactly 0 (d10017ce). Check residual_variance before trusting a very small p_value. Pinned by StatisticsTests.FitMixed_AnExactFit_IsReportedFitted_WithRoundingLevelVariance.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Examples


# mzLib's own reference input (120 simulated features, 29 samples in 7 groups of unequal size;
# `wp` is constant within each group, `age` varies within them), and nlme's output for it:
data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR")
fit <- stats_fit_mixed(file.path(data, "lmm_reference_responses.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "lmm_reference_design.tsv"), file.path(data, "lmm_reference_groups.tsv"),
  c("Intercept", "age", "wp"))
fit
#> <mzlibr_mixed_model_fit> 120 features x 29 samples in 7 groups (group), reml, reporting Intercept, age, wp
#>   fitted 120, too_few_observations 0, rank_deficient 0, too_few_groups 0, variance_ratio_at_limit 0, not_converged 0
# `wp` is a group-level covariate, so it is tested on the groups, not the samples:
table(fit$records$df[fit$records$coefficient == "wp"])
#> 
#>   4   5 
#>   1 119
